title: Construct Quad Tree
summary: Represent a binary square grid as a quad tree.

contractDetails.constraints: The grid is n×n with n = 2^x and 0 ≤ x ≤ 6. All cells are 0 or 1. QuadNode contains boolean val and isLeaf plus the four named child pointers. Leaves have no children. Fixtures serialize records [path,isLeaf,val], starting with path 1 and using child paths 4p,4p+1,4p+2,4p+3 in the stated quadrant order. Output record order is ignored. Internal val is ignored.
contractDetails.output-checking: Invoke construct(grid) to obtain a QuadNode root. Reject cycles, sharing, null internal children, leaf children, and depth greater than six before serializing [path,isLeaf,val] records. Require the correct partition shape and leaf values. Ignore record order and internal-node val.

statement: Represent a binary square grid as a quad tree. A uniform square becomes one leaf whose val is its cell value. A mixed square becomes an internal node with four children for its top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right quarters. An internal val may be either boolean. Return the constructed root.

examples.explanation: One cell is represented by one leaf.
The root is mixed. Its four single-cell quadrants are leaves.
The entire square is uniform and needs no children.

constraints: The grid is n×n with n = 2^x and 0 ≤ x ≤ 6. All cells are 0 or 1. QuadNode contains boolean val and isLeaf plus the four named child pointers. Leaves have no children. Fixtures serialize records [path,isLeaf,val], starting with path 1 and using child paths 4p,4p+1,4p+2,4p+3 in the stated quadrant order. Output record order is ignored. Internal val is ignored.
hints: Conceptual: Large uniform regions need no smaller nodes.
Directional: Split a mixed square into four equal quarters.
Implementation: Test uniformity, return a leaf when all cells agree, and otherwise construct each quarter and attach the four returned roots.
complexityAnalysis: O(n² log n) time and O(log n) call stack space for scanning regions, excluding O(n²) output nodes.
